Radio to Gamma

This right here is the most likely. Microwave ovens use microwave frequency radio waves, while hot objects put out infrared "heat," et cetera. Very high power strobe lights or lasers also fall into this range, and they can start fires, too.

For what it's worth, how hot something gets when it's exposed to this kind of radiation isn't just a function of the type and power of radiation, but also how well the target material absorbs said radiation. Matte black finishes are good for absorbing heat, lighter colors and mirror finishes are bad.
Take combustible material, a magnifying glass and the sun, and there you go: radiations can indeed start a fire.
You also need oxygen though, that wouldn't work in a vaccum.
